context: PR 6972 changes how the sweep crate (extrude, loft, revolve) builds the planes and directions it stores: caps and walls now take their normal, origin and u_ref from the sketch frame carried by the placement, instead of fitting a Newell plane to the built vertices. A cap's origin becomes the carried sketch origin and a line wall's origin becomes its segment's start vertex; the Newell and CapPlane machinery and its refusals are deleted, and new helpers (`Course`, `Sweep`, `Placing::direction`, `sketch_direction`, `section_centre`) are added. The PR claims every stored direction equals main's fitted one at f64, that over an epsilon box the caps and walls are stored exactly, and that the ratified sweep README now holds that no sweep divides a difference of two placed points by its length. It re-baselines a number of committed test rows whose pins moved with the new origins, pins one viewer row red with a filed cause, and keeps the vector-extrusion strut as disclosed. Its body states that hosted CI runs the slow test set and cites a render run and switch-off counts. Both head-versus-base differentials found stored normals, u_refs and carriers equal to the base within 1e-12 or better across 33 and 59 f64 builds, with only plane origins differing.

items.title: PlaneDistance selector returns different faces after carrier origins moved
items.where: editor-core names/geompred.rs:145-155, names/interrogate.rs:374-381 (`entity_point`); pncad-py tests/test_document.py:1028-1033; test_selectors.py:93-96
items.what: `GeomPred::PlaneDistance` measures a face at its carrier origin, which its doc says need not lie on the entity. A line wall's origin moved from its quad centroid (mid-height) to its start vertex (the floor), and a cap's to the sketch origin. On a 1 m cube, "faces more than 0.9 m behind the top" went from the floor to the floor plus four walls; "faces 0.5 above the floor" no longer finds the walls. A wall's answer depends on its segment's start end and sweep direction.
items.evidence: Read from the code and the rewritten Python test, which now asserts 5. No work/ row names it; the body presents it as a test adaptation; test_selectors.py:93-96 still says wall origins are centroids.
items.consequence: Users of this public selector get different face sets for the same query. Pose doors read normal and offset only (eval/wire/pose.rs:666-674), so mates are unaffected.

items.title: Vector-extrusion walls keep a computed, normalized normal with no pinning row
items.what: On the vector arm the wall normal is `place.direction(d).cross(dir).normalize()` with `dir = v.normalize()`, a computed vector divided by its own length. No row pins it over a box and no work/ file schedules it; the body discloses the kept strut, not the wall width. Two probes give different results: over z in [0.95, 1.05] at `Sym<Interval>` the body builds, caps exact, all four wall normals of width 0.403, as on base; over z in [1.95, 2.05] and its negative it refuses at EndpointEnd on both trees.
items.evidence: Both measured by probes on head and base; refusal widths [0, 0.100] head, [0, 0.156] base.
items.consequence: Where the boxed vector extrusion builds, its walls store normals of width 0.403. No document path uses `Vector` (one tour call), so the reach is the public door.

items.title: README clause forbidding difference-over-length divisions is contradicted by loft code
items.what: The ratified README states that no sweep divides the difference of two placed points by its own length, and that walls, rims and struts take the frame turning a direction the sketch holds. Loft struts use `EdgeCurveSpec::line_between` (loft.rs:1326, 1344) and `mev_line` (loft.rs:1513), and the hole bridge uses `mev_line` (swept.rs:911); `line_between` computes (p1 - p0)/|p1 - p0|. The vector-arm wall normal and `sketch_direction` also divide a computed vector by its length.
items.evidence: Read from the code. The body lists loft struts under "looked at, not filed"; no work/ file schedules them.
items.consequence: A ratified design clause states something the code does not do. The struts are scaffolds restated or killed before rest and no frame holds a loft strut's direction; the README sentence carries no "at rest" qualifier.

items.title: Washer registration row removed; replacement row does not test the identity
items.what: The deleted row pinned that the identity the registration discharged is a theorem at `Sym`. The replacement asserts an exact unit `u_ref` and a build; a build that decides the endpoint numerically passes it. The replacement claim ("door open and shut read 497/457") exists in prose and an allowlist script only. Every new revolve row is on `SketchPlane::xy()`.
items.evidence: Symbolic/numeric/frozen counts measured on the washer fixture: full revolve head 501/461/24, base 501/461/36; partial revolve head 493/611/227, base 501/613/221. The numeric count did not rise.
items.consequence: No test would go red if the washer identity fell to a numeric decision, and no revolve row tests a frame other than xy.

items.title: Comments and crate docs still describe the deleted Newell and CapPlane machinery
items.where: sweep lib.rs:14, 131-135; revolve/partial.rs:9; revolve/mod.rs:747, 759, 1134; revolve/tube.rs:472; topo/src/geometry.rs:24; euler.rs:283
items.what: The sweep crate doc's Caps bullet (lib.rs:131-135) still describes caps as `geom_brep::newell_plane` over vertices and apexes flipped by winding, and lib.rs:14 says "Newell-certified cap planes". revolve/mod.rs:747 and 759 refer to "the CapPlane posture"; extrude's copies of that wording were updated and revolve's were not. mod.rs:1134 mentions "Newell failures". tube.rs:472 cites the cap-plane Newell fit as an observed downstream refusal, which no longer exists. topo geometry.rs:24 and euler.rs:283 carry similar text.

items.title: Overlap with PR 6953: conflicts, unequal probe copies, duplicate helper names
items.where: PR 6953; swept.rs; both mesh probes; four editor-core pin files; `Placing::vector` / `Placing::direction`
items.what: A trial merge with PR 6953 conflicts in 7 files (swept.rs in 3 hunks, both mesh probes, four editor-core ledgers). The mesh probe edits are not byte-identical: 6953 moved later and assertion messages differ. `Placing::vector` (6953) and `Placing::direction` (here) are one act under two names. The body names `register_placed_line_end`, which exists nowhere (6953 removed it). One reading finds nothing beyond the conflicts; another finds two more spots needing hand work: 6953's new swept.rs rows call the six-argument form, and 6953's `q_to` row merges in open.
items.evidence: Shown with `git merge-tree`, `git grep` and `git diff`.
items.consequence: Whichever PR merges second needs manual resolution in at least 7 files, and the body's statements about the overlap do not match the trees.

items.title: Cause stated for the pinned ring row's mesh change is disputed
items.what: The ring row's mesh flipped about the vertex (1.48 - 0.031 to 1.48 + 0.031) while `u_ref` is unchanged. The filing says a planar face is triangulated in its chart, whose origin is now the sketch frame's. One reading: a chart-origin translation moved the mesh, so the triangulator is translation-sensitive and the filing is accurate. Another: planar.rs re-derives the chart from boundary points without reading the stored plane, so the stated cause is absent; ulp moves flipping a near-degenerate diagonal are offered, not traced.
items.evidence: Both readings are from the code; u_ref equality is from a differential. The pin passed at three epsilons in CI.
items.consequence: If the second reading holds, the filing's closing condition targets a mechanism that is not present; if the first holds, the mesher has an undiagnosed translation sensitivity.

items.title: Containment test rows cover few parameters and accept wide enclosures
items.what: Every containment row varies one parameter, checking 5 members including both ends; the `spread > vertex_box()` guard is real. No row boxes a revolve angle, a loft placement, the vector arm, two parameters at once, or a revolve off `xy()`. `assert_holds_its_members` has no upper bound on enclosure width, so a degraded enclosure passes. At epsilon 1e-12, `ROUNDING` is 1e-14 and `vertex_box()` is 1.56e-14, so a midpoint-only enclosure escapes by 5e-15.
items.evidence: Read from the tests. Added probe rows (boxed frame under extrude and revolve, boxed loft tilt and height, boxed revolve angle, hole loop, Against) found zero escape with five members.
items.consequence: A regression that widens a varying datum's enclosure, or one in the uncovered doors, would not turn any committed row red; the macroscopic turned-frame row is the one with margin.

items.title: section_centre re-implements the deleted Newell centroid as a vertex mean
items.what: `section_centre` reports the unweighted mean of collapsed vertices and apexes, reproducing the old Newell origin, so `revolved_caps` keeps reporting the value base reported. The value depends on how the loop is cut, which is the reason given for rejecting ruling (B). A circle authored as two unequal arcs would not report its centre. `joints` sits beside caps that state their own origin.
items.evidence: A probe found `revolved_caps` equal to base within 1e-9 on 13 partial revolves. The two-arc circle case was read from the code, not built.
items.consequence: The reported joint depends on authoring choices rather than the section's geometry. The only consumer is the tour's lily, on a full circle.

items.title: Unit-direction invariant held by comment, not by type
items.what: The doc states that "a rigid frame carries a unit direction to a unit direction", but `Placing::direction` returns `Vec3`, and `sketch_direction`, `Course::dir`, `wall_normal` and `cap_plane` pass bare `Vec2`/`Vec3`. Carriers take these as unit. `UnitVec3` exists and is unwrapped at extrude.rs:786.
items.evidence: Read from the code.
items.consequence: Nothing in the types prevents a non-unit vector reaching a carrier that assumes a unit one; the invariant rests on the comment.

items.title: "Decided once" sketch direction is recomputed at each use site
items.what: `sketch_direction`'s doc says the direction is decided once, but it is computed again at the bottom rim, the top rim and the wall, and per loft section; the line's length is computed a second time beside it. The sites call the same function, so they get the same value, and they form one Sym node because Sym hashes content.
items.evidence: Read from the code.
items.consequence: Agreement between the sites holds by convention and by content hashing; the structure does not enforce a single decision.

items.title: Revolved.joints is an Option guarded by unreachable!
items.what: `Revolved.joints` is an `Option` that only the `Partial` kind sets, and the code reaches it through an `unreachable!` on `None` for a partial. Carrying the field on the kind would make the missing case unrepresentable.
items.evidence: Read from the code.
items.consequence: A future path that builds a partial revolve without joints would panic at run time instead of failing to compile.

items.title: Survey's "not re-verified site by site" and other deferred items unscheduled
items.what: The body says the survey's classification was "not re-verified site by site", and no work/ file schedules that verification. Also without a schedule: "about 230 readers out of scope", `torus_radial`, enum-carried directions and description payloads from the blind spot, the slow set, the kept vector-arm geometry and the loft struts.
items.evidence: Searched work/ for rows covering these items; none found. `extrude-arc-walls...` concerns a different question.
items.consequence: Work the PR defers has no tracker entry, so nothing records that it is owed.

items.title: Rewritten mate_tool_flow assertion does not distinguish copy from master
items.what: The old comparison `|underside.x - cap.x| < SHELF_LENGTH` tested the authored x and could not tell copy 1 from the master, since the rest fixes only the plane. The new assertion reads the picked copy's own face through the new origin convention. It would also hold if the mate had read the master; the assertion that discriminates is at :473-480. The new assertion also ties the test to the origin convention.
items.evidence: Read from the test; the row's history was not read.
items.consequence: The rewritten row does not test which copy the mate used, and would change if the origin convention changed again.

items.title: sketch_direction re-derives a direction the profile already records
items.what: `sketch_direction` divides a difference of sketch points by its length (two normalizes), although the profile on this head already records the directions. The change that removes re-derivation from built geometry re-derives one level down. The body discloses it as an interim seam, and a work/ file schedules the replacement.
items.evidence: Read from the code and the tracker file.
items.consequence: Sweep directions come from point differences rather than recorded values until the scheduled change lands; it is one of the falsifiers of the README clause in row 5.

items.title: Course::wall_normal states one rule in two different forms
items.what: The wall normal is d x dir on both arms, but the depth arm writes it as a right normal and the vector arm as cross-then-normalize. Only the doc says the two match.
items.evidence: Read from the code; whether the two forms differ in any case was not tested.

items.title: register_placed_carrier_end proof text covers only radial equal to place
items.what: The function's doc reasons about `u_ref` coming from `sketch_direction` through `place`. `placed_segment_spec_about` passes a separate `radial` placing (full.rs:889). The proof in the doc covers the case `radial == place` only.
items.evidence: Read from the code.
items.consequence: The documented argument does not cover the call path that passes a different radial placing; that path's behaviour was not tested.

items.title: Sketch origin far from profile raises carrier residuals; one cell now refuses
items.what: A line rim now ends at q_from + |b - a| * place(d) instead of the placed far vertex, missing by the placement's rounding, about u times the sketch coordinate. On a turned frame, edge-end residual went 0 to 1.6e-13 and plane/vertex residual 3e-15 to 3.4e-13 at origin distance 1.4e3; 1.5e-12 at 1.4e4; 1.4e-10 at 1.4e6. The 1e8 m mesh probes' new `ResidualExceeded` has the same mechanism.
items.evidence: Measured by probe on head and base. At epsilon 1e-12 a cell at 4.2e3 built on base and refuses on head (`AnalyticRung3(KernelLimit { operand: Plane, bound: 1.8e-12 })`).
items.consequence: Inside the 1e3 m session box nothing flips, but a third of epsilon is spent where none was. No row has a profile away from its sketch origin; the in-box case is not filed.

items.title: Loft with tilted top: mesh volume differs between base and head
items.where: loft with a tilted top; mesh output
items.what: For a loft with a tilted top, the mesh volume differs by 3.3e-7 relative between base and head, while every stored surface and carrier is equal within 1e-9. The cause was not traced; mesh sensitivity to ulp changes is the offered explanation.

items.title: Measure lever and census bound grow with origin-to-face distance
items.what: The measure lever and the census bound scale with the distance between a carrier's origin and its face. Since cap origins are now the sketch origin and wall origins the start vertex, that distance can be larger than before. The bounds remain valid but are wider.
items.evidence: Read from the code.
items.consequence: Measurements and census checks on faces whose origin is far from the face use looser bounds than before.

items.title: Duplicated dispatch and two sources for one frame or turn
items.what: `extrusion` is matched twice in extrude.rs:789-845, once for `(w, course)` and again for `length`. In revolve/mod.rs:532-544 a `Pose` takes its origin from `joints` and its axis from the face. `Placing::point` turns by Rodrigues' formula while `Placing::carry` uses the anchored motion, two spellings of one turn.
items.evidence: Read from the code; whether the two turn spellings ever give different results was not tested.
items.consequence: These are code-form issues: each rule has two places whose agreement is kept by hand.
